attempts.summary: Implemented an Ansible playbook (/home/antrieb/ansible/site.yml on node1) that installs rootless Podman on RHEL7 node1 and runs an httpd:2.4-alpine container as the unprivileged appsvc account on port 8080, starting at boot while appsvc has no active login session. Since RHEL7's systemd 219 lacks the user@.service unit (no persistent systemd --user manager, so loginctl linger cannot start a user service without a login session), the playbook uses a root-owned system unit (webapp.service) with User=appsvc/Group=appsvc, a systemd RuntimeDirectory providing XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, and a persisted sysctl (user.max_user_namespaces) enabling rootless user namespaces. Verified across two full node1 reboots: after the first, the not-yet-persisted sysctl reset and broke the service; this was fixed by persisting it in /etc/sysctl.d and re-running the (idempotent) playbook. After the second reboot the service came up automatically with no manual steps: HTTP 200 on port 8080, webapp.service active, container running as appsvc via podman/slirp4netns, and `who`/`w` showing 0 users. node2 (Ubuntu, outside task scope) was also restarted per the mandatory protocol, with a confirmed boot-id change and healthy systemd state.
